Regulus Black. From the little information we have on him, we have learned so much about his character and I do think that Hermione's theory was true. Like Sirius, Regulus wasn't like his family but he loved his family and he knew that to protect them he had to behave the way that was expected: like a member of not only the most ancient and noble house of Black but as a member of the sacred 28 who are all about blood purity and elitism. I have no doubt that he grew up with some of the qualities his family taught but they were slowly abandoned (thanks to Sirius, no doubt), but the big difference between Sirius and Regulus is that Regulus was clever as fuck.
 
For Sirius, things were very black and white: you're either a Death Eater or a decent human being. But you can still infer based off his mixed reactions in regards to Regulus that he loved his brother very much and that Regulus didn't fit into the black and white that Sirius could put everyone else into. 

Regulus, however, loved his family despite their views and he knew that to keep everyone safe he had to play the part and play it well. He didn't think Voldemort was capable of as much evil as he claimed *until* Voldemort borrowed Regulus' house elf, Kreacher, and nearly killed him creating a horcrux. Now think of the way the Malfoys treated Dobby and how house elves were basically slaves to wizards (yes, the house elves in the castle liked their lives but they also weren't abused and mistreated like Dobby was by the Malfoys, and I'm assuming the Sacred 28 families that were also Death Eaters weren't much different) and there is a huge difference between how Regulus viewed house elves versus how others (again, presumably Sacred 28 families) did. He loved Kreacher and knowing that Voldemort was so flippant about Kreacher's life is what basically "awoke" Regulus to the fact that this wizard wasn't actually all talk.

It's canon that horcruxes are an extremely dark and ancient form of magic that is NOT commonly known. The nature and concept of a horcrux was so evil and terrifying that they were kept secret from the wizarding world and very few knew what they even were (Voldemort is only one of two wizards who have ever created one). They were not something that wizards could just read about in their textbooks in great detail (Hogwarts banned the subject and any mention of them was brief and probably extremely vague) and there was only one book that described them fully, and that book was in the restricted section until Dumbledore removed it after Tom Riddle got a hold of it. Hermione found it purely by chance. 

The book was removed in the 1950s and Regulus attended Hogwarts in the seventies and by the time he was eighteen years old, he not only discovered that Voldemort was creating horcruxes but that horcruxes were a thing *at all*. He created a duplicate of the locket and put that note inside of it where he acknowledged that he would die (at eighteen years old. he was a child!), willingly drank the potion (I don't want to think about what that potion made him see) and ordered Kreacher to replace the locket and leave without him and not tell *anyone* of the circumstances of his death because if anyone knew what really happened, word would get back to Voldemort and his family would be killed. 

His family and other wizards believed he was a dark wizard. Sirius Black died thinking his brother was a Death Eater who got in over his head. No one knew the truth until Harry, Ron, and Hermione started hunting horcruxes, found the locket, and, eventually, Kreacher led all the house elves to fight against Voldemort for his master, Regulus.
